name: Baeyer-Villiger oxidation: acetone + performic acid -> methyl acetate + formic acid (acid-catalyzed)

prompt.query: Determine the mechanism of the following reaction: Baeyer-Villiger oxidation: acetone + performic acid -> methyl acetate + formic acid (acid-catalyzed). Reactant SMILES: [OH3+].CC(C)=O.O=COO; product SMILES: [OH3+].CC(=O)OC.O=CO; total charge 1, multiplicity 1; conditions: peracid, inert solvent; acid-catalyzed (H3O+ written into the SMILES on both sides). Atom-mapped reactant SMILES: [OH2+:1]([H:10]).[CH3:2][C:3](=[O:4])[CH3:5].[CH:6](=[O:7])[O:8][O:9][H:11]. The 1-based map numbers in it are the indexing convention for `bond_changes` (keep using the plain SMILES above for graph nodes and evidence annotations). The reaction may proceed through a multi-step network: represent each intermediate you identify as a node and each elementary step as an edge; competing pathways you investigate deserve their own edges. You must maintain `mechanism_graph.json` in the sandbox root recording the mechanism graph: nodes (reactant/intermediate/product/transition_state, with SMILES) and elementary-step edges (with `via` pointing to the TS node id). Start the graph at the reactant complex (the pre-reaction complex), not at the separated reactants. The scorer checks that your graph covers the reference mechanism as a subgraph: extra nodes or edges beyond the reference are never penalized, so record every step you actually investigated. Every elementary-step edge must carry `bond_changes`: `break`/`form` lists of [i, j] atom-map index pairs, where [i, j] belongs to `break` if the bond order between atoms i and j decreases over the step (including full cleavage) and to `form` if it increases (including newly formed bonds); a purely conformational or inversion step carries two empty lists. The scorer reads this file forensically; a missing or unparseable file severely impacts the score. Every computational evidence file you produce for a species or step (QM input or log) must carry a `smiles: <SMILES>` comment line identifying the species, so the scorer can bind each graph element to concrete evidence. In your final summary you must report the computed barrier in kcal/mol for the rate-determining step, relative to the reactant complex (the pre-reaction complex, e.g. the ion-dipole complex of a bimolecular reaction; for a unimolecular process this is simply the reactant minimum). Run the computations with ORCA or Gaussian: the scorer parses only these two programs' log formats, so output from any other program cannot count as evidence. Allowed computational methods are limited to MACE-OMol25 and xTB; calls beyond the whitelist are intercepted.

system.conditions: peracid, inert solvent; acid-catalyzed (H3O+ written into the SMILES on both sides)

edges.step_type: carbonyl oxygen protonation by hydronium (PT, pre-equilibrium)
performic acid terminal oxygen addition to the protonated carbonyl -> protonated Criegee tetrahedral intermediate (rate-determining per computation)
1,2-methyl migration to the terminal oxygen concerted with O-O cleavage and proton shuffle onto the departing formate oxygen -> protonated methyl acetate + formic acid
deprotonation of the ester carbonyl by water, regenerating H3O+ (PT)
